title: ChatGPT scaffolding in supporting metacognition for limit concepts in guided inquiry mathematics learning
venue: Journal of Information Technology Education: Research
extended_summary:
This study examines how ChatGPT-mediated scaffolding can support students’ metacognitive development while learning limit concepts in calculus through a guided inquiry approach. The paper is motivated by the challenge that students often struggle with planning, monitoring, and evaluating their problem-solving in abstract mathematics, and by the question of whether generative AI can serve as a metacognitive partner rather than merely a tool for getting answers. The authors focus on systematic integration of ChatGPT within inquiry-based mathematics learning and on the scaffolding patterns that emerge during student-AI interactions.

The intervention was implemented with 75 undergraduate mathematics education students enrolled in Calculus I at Universitas Jambi, Indonesia. Over four weeks and six 120-minute sessions, students worked through guided inquiry activities on limit concepts with support from ChatGPT and instructor guidance. Two experienced mathematics lecturers, both of whom received specialized training in integrating ChatGPT into guided inquiry, facilitated the activities. Data sources included pre/post metacognitive assessments, a limit concept test, screen recordings of 180 hours of ChatGPT interactions, reflective journals, and interviews.

The study finds that ChatGPT-supported guided inquiry was associated with significant gains in metacognitive skills, especially monitoring and evaluation, as well as improved conceptual understanding of limits. The analysis identifies six scaffolding patterns: prior knowledge activation, guided exploration, structured analysis, critical evaluation, independent application, and metacognitive reflection. These patterns suggest that ChatGPT can help students connect everyday examples to formal mathematics, generate and test hypotheses, analyze representations, and reflect on their reasoning. However, the paper also notes that a substantial minority of students passively accepted AI-generated answers, indicating that learning outcomes depend heavily on structured prompts, teacher mediation, and explicit instruction in critical questioning. The authors conclude that ChatGPT is most effective when embedded in a carefully designed guided inquiry framework that preserves student agency and supports reflective mathematical thinking.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed convergent mixed-methods study, but it is not a randomized controlled trial and relies on a single-group pre-post design with qualitative coding. The evidence is informative but limited by the absence of a comparison group and potential selection/implementation effects.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects are modest-to-large for metacognition and positive for limit learning, with effect sizes around d=0.78-0.88 and a mean learning gain of 0.82. The study is on a specific undergraduate mathematics population rather than a broad K-12 group, so the broader impact is promising but not definitive.

interventions.use_case: ChatGPT-mediated scaffolding in guided inquiry mathematics learning for limit concepts, using dialogic prompts, iterative feedback, and reflective questioning to support metacognition and problem solving.

finding.finding_summary: Students showed significant gains in understanding limit concepts after the four-week ChatGPT-supported guided inquiry intervention (n=75). The paper reports a mean improvement of 0.82 (p < .001) on the Limit Concept Assessment, with stronger performance especially in conceptual and procedural limit tasks.
finding.measure: Limit Concept Assessment (LCA), 20-item test of procedural and conceptual understanding of limits

finding.finding_summary: Metacognitive skills improved significantly over the intervention, with the largest gains in monitoring (d = 0.85), followed by evaluation (d = 0.82) and planning (d = 0.78). Across 180 hours of interaction data, students shifted from procedural queries toward more investigative and reflective questioning, indicating stronger self-regulated problem solving.
finding.measure: Metacognitive Awareness Inventory (MAI) and coded ChatGPT-student interaction patterns
finding.effect_size: d=0.85 (monitoring), d=0.82 (evaluation), d=0.78 (planning); overall d=0.85 reported for metacognitive skills
